name: H.E.S.S.
summary: Ground-based stereoscopic imaging Cherenkov array searching the Galactic center, dwarf galaxies and unidentified gamma-ray sources for dark-matter annihilation.
detection_principle: Multiple mirror telescopes image atmospheric Cherenkov light from gamma rays simultaneously, reconstructing direction and energy and rejecting hadronic backgrounds.

status.label: Operation supported by evidence
status.evidence: The institution's current page describes operation and science plans. No separate 2026 status announcement was established, so the date remains null.

key_parameters.name: Array
key_parameters.value: 4 telescopes of 12 m aperture + 1 telescope of 28 m aperture

key_parameters.name: Representative energy band
key_parameters.value: 50 GeV–100 TeV, depending on analysis selections

phases.name: H.E.S.S. II
phases.description: Addition of the large central telescope

results.summary: Tests unidentified Fermi sources as dark subhalos; results require interpretation alongside the astrophysical properties of each source.

science_scope: Tests dark-matter models through astrophysical radiation, cosmic rays or neutrinos. Astrophysical backgrounds and propagation models affect interpretation; an anomaly alone does not establish dark matter.
